prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules induce proximity between a target protein and a ubiquitin ligase, from the first PROTACs to the cereblon-dependent action of thalidomide-class molecular glues.

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation is the one shortlisted achievement where a biological process, regulated protein turnover, was converted into a defined chemical event: a small molecule forms a ternary complex and a ubiquitin ligase tags the target. The principle has been reproduced independently with many ligases, many targets and many chemotypes, and the ternary-complex cooperativity can be measured quantitatively. It is the only candidate that every member lists somewhere, and four members already prefer it. After the first round I think a single-achievement prize with Crews, Deshaies and Handa is better than my earlier two-part proposal, because the cereblon result is what connects the PROTAC concept to molecular glues and to the mechanism of thalidomide, and the three-name cap is respected.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC drug is approved as far as I know, and I have not verified this independently, so clinical vindication is incomplete. A single citation may read as two discoveries joined together, since the PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies) and the cereblon glue mechanism (Handa) have different origins. Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim are left out, and the omission of Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures is a real cost. Handa's contribution is largely target identification by affinity purification, so the chemical novelty is less obvious than for the PROTAC concept.

responses.point: Aili argues that Liu alone would pass over Komor, Gaudelli and Kondo and Nishida, and that base editing leans on a platform the 2020 prize already honoured, whereas degradation introduces a new small-molecule pharmacology.
responses.response: I accept this and it is the main reason I changed my configuration. In round 1 I defended Liu as sole credit, but five members dispute that attribution, and I cannot show that the cytosine and adenine editors are the work of one person. A fair base-editing citation would need Liu, Komor and Gaudelli at least, and Kondo and Nishida's independent report would still be unresolved. That is more names than the cap allows beside a second part. You also argued that Handa should hold the third place in B044, and I now agree.

responses.point: Linke says the molecular-glue half is hard to defend without cereblon, and that he is unsure whether swapping Ciulli for Handa is the right trade. He also doubts Liu alone is the best use of a slot.
responses.response: On the chair's question about Handa, I would put it this way: the PROTAC concept alone would not explain why thalidomide-class drugs degrade neosubstrates. Cereblon as the direct target is a measured, reproducible result that explains the glue mechanism, so I see Handa as part of the same achievement, induced proximity to a ubiquitin ligase, rather than a staple. I still do not claim Handa's work is PROTAC chemistry, and the citation should say so by naming the cereblon-dependent action separately. I share your unease about leaving Ciulli out, but I cannot find a version of the cap that keeps Ciulli without dropping Deshaies or Handa.

responses.point: Aqvist says that sole credit to Liu sits uneasily with the decisive experiments of Komor and Gaudelli, and that base editing looks like a tool built on the already rewarded CRISPR platform. He puts degradation ahead.
responses.response: I argued in round 1 that the deaminase mechanism makes base editing chemically distinct from Cas9 cleavage, and I still think so. But distinct chemistry does not settle attribution, and on that you are right. I drop B019 from my preferred configuration and keep it only as an alternative. On the approval question you raised, my view is unchanged: reproduction across many laboratories is the evidence I trust, and approval is a clinical milestone, not a test of the mechanism. If the committee prefers to wait, I would not call that unreasonable, but I would not call it disqualifying.

responses.point: Brzezinski prefers nitrogenase for Rees, Einsle and Seefeldt, on the basis of a cofactor structure confirmed over about three decades and a physically explicit mechanism.
responses.response: The chair asked whether a citation can rest on structure and cofactor function alone. I think it can, because the FeMo-cofactor and its carbide are established by independent crystallography. But your own case_against concedes that the E4 state, the substrate site and the order of proton and electron delivery are open, and a citation naming mechanism would claim more than has been measured. A structure-only citation would be defensible, but it also leaves the Dean-Seefeldt attribution question open. I keep B032 as an alternative, and I would move it up if the degradation vote stalls and your structure-only framing is adopted.

responses.point: Sparr prefers phase separation and notes that it may not reach five votes. The chair asks which predictions of the framework are confirmed in living cells and not only in vitro.
responses.response: My answer to the chair's question is that I have not seen quantitative confirmation at endogenous concentrations for most condensates, so my view from round 1 is unchanged. I take the point that the multivalency framework is a real physical-chemical principle in vitro. For me the open point is which in-cell structures are true phases. I would be glad to be shown measurements that settle it, but until then I place B039 below degradation.

uncertainties: Whether a single citation can join PROTACs and cereblon-dependent glues without implying that Handa's work is PROTAC chemistry.
How much weight the absence of an approved PROTAC drug should carry this year; I have not verified the claim independently.
Whether Handa or Ciulli is the better third name, and how the committee should weigh the omission of Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim.
Whether base editing can be credited cleanly at all, given Liu, Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida and the question of prime editing (B049).
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. I have no known personal or institutional link to the credited candidates for B044, B019 or B032. Umeå nucleotide-metabolism research is not connected to any of them to my knowledge.
